## Orientation

The recorder records the way a careful learner moves through a workbook. This orientation block is deliberately tall enough to make the activity band enter the viewport from below instead of appearing already docked at the top.

A learner first scans the setup. They look at the part title, the lesson title, and this block, then continue only when the next surface is ready. The video should show that flow rather than jumping straight into hidden state.

The next paragraphs add realistic texture for deterministic motion analysis. The text repeats the shape of tutorial prose: a short claim, a concrete instruction, and a reminder that feedback should stay attached to the surface that produced it.

When the editor appears, the learner will type a draft, pause, read feedback, adjust the draft, and pause again. The recorder needs that feedback to arrive while the activity band is in the flow of the page, docked at the top, and below the fold after the learner has scrolled away.

When the terminal appears, the learner will type commands one character at a time into the real xterm input path. The fake shell will echo output and emit the same authoritative workbook command markers that Bash emits in production.

The activity band keeps one shape. It sits in the workbook column, sticks to the top of the viewport when the learner scrolls past it, and never changes size with the scroll position. Feedback must land on it without moving the page in any of those states.

Continue when you are ready to open the editor practice.
